title: Book Three · Chapter 144: Three New Saturdays
story:
Two school weeks remain before the winter holiday.

On Friday, Ronan stops at Mr Sun's after school. Dad has left his lunch cloth at home, and Ronan has brought it back.

Mr Sun is checking the coming Saturdays. Another worker needs time for family visits. There will still be customers at the front.

“Could you help for three mornings?” he asks Ronan.

Ronan puts Dad's cloth beside his bag.

“Which three?”

Mr Sun points to the dates. The first is tomorrow. The second is the following Saturday. The third is the first Saturday of the winter holiday.

“Nine until twelve. Two yuan each morning, paid at the end.”

“At twelve each Saturday?”

“Yes.”

Ronan looks at the three dates again. He has school work, but he can do it in the afternoons. No visit is in his notebook for those days.

“I can do those three.”

Mr Sun turns the book toward him so he can read each line.

Ronan follows the dates with his finger. The last one is in the holiday. He has not put any visit beside it.

“The same front jobs?” he asks.

“Papers and customers. Ask me about the finished pieces before they leave.”

“And the prices?”

“Leave those with me.”

Ronan nods. He knows more of the shelves now, but he does not know the cost of every kind of wood.

Mr Sun shows him the open space in the work book. The other helper's name is beside the mornings before these. There is no name beside the three new ones yet.

Ronan reads the hours again. He can do his own school work after lunch. He will need to begin it then, instead of leaving it for Sunday.

“Do you need a copy?” Mr Sun asks.

“Yes, please.”

Ronan takes out his notebook. He wants the same three dates in both places before he goes home.

Mr Sun writes the agreement in his book. Ronan copies the dates and times for himself.

Dad comes to the front with an empty cup.

“More paper?”

“Three mornings of it,” Ronan says.

“The pencil will be pleased.”

Ronan laughs. Mr Sun takes a long pencil from the counter and holds it up.

“The old one has retired.”

The next morning, Ronan arrives before nine. He starts with the front papers, then checks the small finished pieces with Mr Sun.

A man brings a drawing for a narrow cupboard. Ronan asks about the door and the space above it. He leaves the price line for Mr Sun.

The man puts a finger beside the top.

“I forgot that part.”

He takes the drawing home to add the missing height. Ronan writes his name and the next question together. Before he leaves, the man draws an arrow from the hall. Ronan can now see how the cupboard will go into the room.

At twelve, Mr Sun pays him two yuan. The first of the three mornings is complete.

Ronan puts the money in his work envelope at home. The twenty-one becomes twenty-three.

Mum is resting with her feet near the sunny doorway. He sits on the step beside her and tells her about the retired pencil.

“Did it receive a chair?” she asks.

“A paper box.”

“A quiet life.”

Ronan smiles and stretches his legs. There are two work dates left in his notebook.

He puts it on his shelf before he eats lunch. Afterward, he opens his school book and starts with the first unfinished question.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

remain＝还剩；agreement＝约定；retire＝退休、停止使用；height＝高度。

## 理解问题

1. 这三次是原暑假工作自动延长吗？新约定的日期、工时与报酬怎样？
2. 本章实际完成了几次、领到多少？工资信封由多少变为多少？

## 读句子

**There are two work dates left in his notebook.**

拆开看：There are / two work dates left / in his notebook.

还有／两个待工作的日期／记在他的本子里。
